notes: Outputs are verbatim AWS CLI JSON objects, not raw HTTP bytes. Modeled errors captured using --cli-error-format json; no debug headers retained. SecretAccessKey is the sole redacted output field. HTTP status omitted unless directly observed.

Calls 14-28 were invalid experiment setup: shared Eval globals replaced table name with a local-engine-only name. No such native resource existed; mutations returned ResourceNotFoundException (empty-set validation happened first). These calls are not evidence about the intended fixture. Replayed under isolated process with correct owned table name.

nativeFacts.fact: Missing Put ALL_OLD, missing Get and missing Delete ALL_OLD returned {}; existing mutation return values and failure Item are captured. N 1.00 normalized to 1, NS normalized and SS ordered in observed response; numeric-vs-string condition failed, invalid numeric ADD on string and empty SS were validation errors. Nested list/map, BOOL and NULL types survived.

Query and Scan Limit applied before filtering. Empty Items with Count 0 and ScannedCount 1 still returned LastEvaluatedKey. Query COUNT matched 2 of 3 in tenant-a; full Scan COUNT scanned 4. COUNT omitted Items.
GSI eventual query succeeded. GSI strong Query and Scan failed ValidationException; missing-index Query also failed ValidationException, not ResourceNotFoundException.
BatchGet omitted missing items; duplicate keys rejected. BatchWrite malformed key and same-key put/delete rejected, and strong Get showed no valid write from malformed mixed request.

Transaction cancellation reasons preserve action order with None placeholders and requested old Items; follow-up transaction read confirmed no partial mutation. Same-token replay incremented only once and changed consumed capacity from write to read; changed payload failed IdempotentParameterMismatchException. Duplicate item transaction rejected.

Quoted hyphenated PartiQL table names succeeded; unquoted failed. Escaped apostrophe string and RETURNING ALL OLD worked. Limit 1 returned both NextToken and LastEvaluatedKey, including filtered empty page; NextToken continued. Batch and transaction mixed reads/writes rejected. Transaction reads preserve order with empty missing-item object; writes returned Responses []; cancellation retained ordered reasons and atomicity.

Real owned user policy allowed projected tenant-a reads, rejected tenant-b LeadingKeys, secret Attributes, no projection and COUNT Select. Nested projection was checked by top-level doc attribute. Mixed BatchGet leading keys rejected as a whole; Scan denied because no Scan action grant.

EnclosingOperation allowed TransactGetItems/ExecuteTransaction while direct GetItem/ExecuteStatement denied on the auxiliary table. FullTableScan explicit denial blocked unkeyed SELECT and non-key WHERE, while partition-key SELECT succeeded.

ownershipAssessment.status: Inference from native contracts, not a measurement of DynamoDB Local
ownershipAssessment.engineCandidate: Item storage/types, expression evaluation, key/index reads, filtering/pagination, batch structural validation, transaction atomicity/cancellation/idempotency, PartiQL execution should be compared with the separate real Local engine experiment before assigning gaps.
ownershipAssessment.frontendIAM: Caller credentials/account/region namespace and resource/action authorization; derive LeadingKeys, top-level Attributes, Select, EnclosingOperation and PartiQL FullTableScan context before executing. Do not infer authorization solely from the outer transaction/PartiQL API name.

uncertainties: No claim about throttling, concurrent transaction conflicts, 10-minute token expiry, 1-MB pagination boundaries, or GSI propagation latency; deliberately not exercised.
Observed set ordering is preserved, not asserted as a stable cross-request/API guarantee.
IAM coverage used read actions; write-specific ReturnValues restrictions and write EnclosingOperation combinations were not established.
PartiQL LeadingKeys/Attributes restrictions were not combined with FullTableScan policy; native calls establish the separate tested policy statements only.
No raw HTTP status was observed because debug transport output was not enabled; modeled CLI JSON errors and outputs are preserved.
